description: Screenshot of a legal reference webpage (dark-mode, consistent with Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute layout) showing the full text of 28 U.S. Code Section 541, United States attorneys. The statute covers presidential appointment of U.S. attorneys with Senate consent, their four-year terms, and their removability by the President.
text: 28 U.S. Code § 541. United States attorneys. U.S. Code. Notes. prev | next. (a) The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, a United States attorney for each judicial district. (b) Each United States attorney shall be appointed for a term of four years. On the expiration of his term, a United States attorney shall continue to perform the duties of his office until his successor is appointed and qualifies. (c) Each United States attorney is subject to removal by the President. (Added Pub. L. 89–554, § 4(c), Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 617.)

description: Screenshot of a Facebook check-in post from an attendee of the June 2020 Trump rally at the BOK Center in Tulsa, Oklahoma, paired with a selfie showing a dense outdoor crowd of rally-goers in red Trump 2020 hats and shirts on a city street. The post claims thousands of ticketed supporters were being kept behind barricades due to a lack of screeners, and disputes reports of a poor turnout. Children are visible in the crowd.
text: Rachel Merton is attending President Trump Rally in Tulsa, Oklahoma at BOK Center. 1 hr · Tulsa. 1000's more supporters with tickets are not being allowed past barricades. Apparently there are no more 'screeners' to let us through the check points. If you hear there's a poor turnout, it's simply not true. #patriot #trump2020

Children visible in crowd photo, unnamed
Turnout/barricade claim is the poster’s unverified claim
